title: Lupus KP Signal Sifter
bodyHtml:
The Signal Sifter allows you to view lupus-associated variants in a genomic region of interest, from an analysis of 7,219 SLE cases and 15,991 controls of European ancestry (Bentham, Morris, et al., 2015), in the context of thousands of tissue-specific genomic annotations. Start by entering a gene name or genomic coordinates (in the format "chr:start-end", e.g. "6:25413381-34403276") in the Set region box below, then click Search.

  • Click on a column header in the tables below to sort the table by that column.
  • Click on the "camera" icon at the upper right of each section to prepare the data in that section for downloading. Then click on the "Data files" icon at the upper right of this page to see the list of the data files you requested and download them in .csv and/or JSON format.
  • To generate a summary of the results you have viewed, click Open Summary Section at the lower right of the page and select the data types you would like to include in the table.

The Associated genes tab displays gene-level associations for SLE with p-value ≤ 0.05, as determined by the MAGMA method. To explore a new region in the Signal Sifter, mouse over coordinates in the View Region column and click Set region.

 

The Genome-wide associations tab displays LD-clumped genome-wide significant (p ≤ 5e-8) associations across the genome. To explore a new region in the Signal Sifter, mouse over coordinates in the Clumped Region column and click Set region.

 

The Associated variants in region tab displays LD-clumped SLE genetic associations in the region you have selected. Filter both the plot and table using the filters below.

 

Clumped Variants description

The plots and table on the Globally Enriched Tissues/Annotations tab display global enrichment of SLE genetic associations within regions annotated in specific tissues as accessible chromatin, binding sites, enhancers, or promoters, as determined by stratified LD score regression. Mouse over the plots to see tissue specificity.

 

The Tissue-level annotations tab displays tissue-specific epigenomic annotations in this region, drawn from the Common Metabolic Diseases Genome Atlas (CMDGA). To see annotations in specific biosamples within a tissue, mouse over a tissue name in the table, click on Set tissue, and then view the Biosample-level annotations tab.

 

The Biosample-level annotations tab displays cell type (biosample)-specific epigenomic annotations in this region for the tissue(s) you have set.

 

The Target gene links tab displays genomic regions that are linked to specific genes by 3-D chromatin interactions in the tissue(s) you have set, discovered by techniques such as ChIP-seq or Hi-C.

 

The SNP to Gene Links tab displays genomic regions that are linked to specific genes by the Combined SNP-to-Gene strategy (Gazal et al., 2022). These links are not tissue-specific.
